newsitem.title: SWAZILAND: Golf-Druian wins first title in Royal Swazi Open.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Druian wins first title in Royal Swazi Open.

text.p: South Africa's Warrick Druian, despite finding the rough at the par-three last, won his first tournament as a professional by one shot in the 1997 Royal Swazi Open on Sunday.
The 27-year-old, who enjoyed a two-shot advantage going into the final round, fired a two-under 70 for a 72-hole total of 269 - 19-under-par for the tournament.
Although Druian only managed three birdies all day - with a solitary drop at the seventh - he was able to resist the pressing challenge of playing partners Chris Davison and Nic Henning.

With a slender one-shot lead playing the 18th, Druian found the rough on the down slope by a greenside bunker with his seven-iron approach. But he coolly managed to get up and down from there to save par - and to secure his maiden professional success
"Standing on that last tee was the only time during the day when I didn't feel in control of the tournament - and I was definitely thinking of a three-way play-off," Druian said later.
"The 18th has been a key hole in this event over the years and I knew it was going to be tough playing it. I pulled my approach left but, thankfully, it was lying fairly decently.
"From there, my sand wedge helped to me get up and down and this victory really is a dream come true."

England-born Davison (with a closing 67) and second-round leader Henning (69) had to settle for a share of second place on 270 after the possibility of a three-way play-off was averted by Druian on the final hole.
Davison had turned in 34 and then gathered four more birdies on the hillier back nine to get to within a shot of Druian playing the last.
Henning, tournament leader after the second round, made a critical birdie-two at the par-three 18th to join Davison at 18-under - but it was not enough to force a play-off.
